n: Who is truly wise and can explain the meaning of things? Wisdom lights up a person’s face and softens a harsh or stern expression.
The Preacher advises obeying the king, partly because of the sacred oath of loyalty taken before God.

f.g: An oath sworn in God’s name, perhaps an oath of allegiance to the king.

n: Don’t storm out of the king’s presence or join a bad cause, since a king can do whatever he wants.

f.w: stand not in an evil thing
f.g: Don’t persist in a wrong course or plot.

n: A king’s word carries authority; no one can challenge him. Wise subjects respect that power.
Those who obey will stay out of trouble, and a wise heart knows the right time and right way to act.
There is a right time and way for everything, yet people suffer because they often don’t know them.
No one knows the future or can tell when things will happen.

f.w: knoweth not that which shall be

n: No one can hold back the breath of life or control the day of death. There’s no release from that battle, and wickedness won’t rescue those who practice it.

f.g: Hold on to the breath of life.
No one is excused from serving in death’s battle.

n: He has watched how people exercise power over others, sometimes to their own harm.
He saw wicked people buried with honor after coming and going from the holy place, and then praised in the city where they did evil. That too is empty.
Because punishment for evil isn’t carried out quickly, people grow bold in doing wrong. Delayed justice can encourage sin.
Even if a sinner does wrong a hundred times and lives long, the Preacher is sure that things will go well for those who reverence God.

f.w: it shall be well with them that fear God

n: But it will not go well for the wicked; his days will pass like a shadow because he refuses to revere God.

f.w: not be well with the wicked

n: Here is a puzzle: sometimes good people suffer what the wicked deserve, and the wicked enjoy what the righteous deserve. Earthly life doesn’t always reflect divine justice.

f.w: according to the work of the wicked

n: So the Preacher recommends enjoying life — eating, drinking, and being glad — as God’s gift that stays with us through our labor.
When he devoted himself to understanding all that goes on in the world, he saw people so busy they barely sleep.

f.w: neither day nor night seeth sleep
f.g: An idiom for restless, sleepless effort.

n: Then he realized that no one can fully understand God’s work. Even the wisest who claim to know cannot discover it all.
